nfl.oneThing: The NFL trade deadline is Tuesday, Nov. 10, and ESPN has ranked the top 25 candidates to move, with Colts running back Jonathan Taylor at No. 1.

headlines.title: Trade deadline less than two weeks away
headlines.summary: The deadline is Tuesday, Nov. 10, at 4 p.m. ET. ESPN's Matt Bowen and Jeremy Fowler have ranked the top 25 possible trade candidates by the value they would give a new team, not by how likely a move is. Taylor is No. 1, and the Colts are being asked whether they would listen on him. Teams Fowler has spoken to aren't convinced Indianapolis will trade him. Several AFC teams are bunched at 4–3 or 3–4 just outside the playoff line.
headlines.whyItMatters: Deals made before the deadline could change the playoff race in both conferences, where the margins are small.

headlines.title: Bills at 5–1 after the bye, eyeing the one seed
headlines.summary: Buffalo are 5–1 and second in the AFC. Losses by New England, Baltimore and Kansas City over the bye have given the Bills a real chance at the conference's top seed. Their last game was a 33–30 win over the Raiders in Week 6, which came down to the wire. A fan survey from SB Nation Reacts says the pass defence has been a recurring problem.
headlines.whyItMatters: Buffalo are in position to claim the AFC's top seed if they keep winning, and the defence is the question that will decide it.

headlines.title: Garrett Wilson wants to win, not necessarily to leave
headlines.summary: Jets receiver Garrett Wilson says he doesn't want to be traded, but he is frustrated by his lack of involvement in the offence and by losing. He was targeted only three times in the 28–25 loss to Miami, catching two for 26 yards. He signed a four-year, $130 million extension through 2030 about 15 months ago. The Jets are 2–5 and face the Raiders in Week 8.
headlines.whyItMatters: With the deadline approaching and the Jets losing, speculation about Wilson's future is likely to continue.

headlines.title: Winless Chargers keep McDaniel as playcaller
headlines.summary: The Chargers are 0–6 and have lost six straight. Coach Jim Harbaugh announced Wednesday that offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel will keep calling the plays. ESPN describes McDaniel as embattled.

contextCard.title: How practice squads work
contextCard.body: A practice squad is a group of extra players who train with a team but are not on the active roster. They can be signed and released more easily than active players, and other teams can sign them away. Practice squad players can also be promoted to the active roster for games. Many of the recent signings in the news are practice squad moves.

nba.oneThing: Tyrese Haliburton will miss at least two weeks with a left hamstring strain, and Anthony Edwards is having knee surgery with his return timetable set in weeks or months.

headlines.title: Haliburton out at least two weeks with hamstring strain
headlines.summary: Pacers guard Tyrese Haliburton has a strained left hamstring and will miss at least the next two weeks, Shams Charania of ESPN reports. He missed all of last season with an Achilles tear and is back on the injury list after only four games. Before the injury he was averaging 9.5 assists per game, second in the league.
headlines.whyItMatters: Indiana are 2–2 and eighth in the East, so how they cope without him will shape their early season.

headlines.title: Edwards to have knee surgery, Wolves expect him back
headlines.summary: The Timberwolves say Anthony Edwards will be 'good as new' after arthroscopic surgery on his right knee, scheduled for Thursday. President of basketball operations Tim Connelly said the timetable for his return, weeks or months, will be clearer after the procedure. An MRI found new damage that earlier scans didn't show. Edwards scored 47 points in an overtime loss at Cleveland and has 133 points through four games, a franchise record. He averages 33.2 points, second in the league.
headlines.whyItMatters: Minnesota are 3–1 and sixth in the West. Their offseason changes were working before the injury, so the early race depends on how they cope.

headlines.title: Ernie Johnson to step away from Inside the NBA
headlines.summary: Ernie Johnson will step away as host of Inside the NBA after this season. He announced the decision in a social media video on Wednesday, saying it was his choice and 'it's just time.' Johnson, 70, is in his 37th year hosting the show. He says he is cutting back rather than retiring, and he has dealt with heart issues in recent years.
headlines.whyItMatters: ESPN says it will celebrate Johnson throughout the season, so this year's show will carry farewell coverage.

headlines.title: Doncic out with back tightness against the Clippers
headlines.summary: Luka Doncic will miss the Lakers' game against the Clippers with back tightness. He scored 41 points, with nine assists and five rebounds, in a 136–129 home loss to Portland on Tuesday, the Lakers' first loss after a 3–0 start. A day earlier he scored 52 points against Utah, tying Kareem Abdul-Jabbar's 10 career 50-point games. He became the fastest player to 3,000 points in a Lakers uniform, doing it in 95 games.
headlines.whyItMatters: The Lakers are 3–1 and fifth in the West. Ziaire Williams is also out with a foot injury, so the depth will be tested.

recaps.keyLine: Reed 22 pts, 9 reb, 3 ast · Cunningham 19 pts, 9 reb, 8 ast · Towns 27 pts, 20 reb, 3 ast · Brunson 23 pts, 1 reb, 7 ast
recaps.text: New York beat Detroit 111–97 to end an 0–3 start and push the Pistons back to 3–1. Karl-Anthony Towns' 20 rebounds were the key, and Jalen Brunson added seven assists. Cade Cunningham had nine rebounds and eight assists for Detroit, but the Pistons' unbeaten start is gone.

Stephon Castle added 15 points, five rebounds and five assists. San Antonio move to 2–2, and Sacramento are still winless at 0–4.
